Telegram Revenge Porn

By: Latashia Naidoo | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The Covid-19 pandemic has seen an alarming global increase in image-based abuse on social media.Locally, insidious Telegram groups have been created to share women's intimate images - without consent.

Unique Selling Point:
Image-based sexual abuse - Inside the Telegram groups spreading revenge porn

Rape videos, revenge porn, and child porn - just some of the content that's being shared on scores of local private Telegram groups which pride themselves at shaming and doxing women, anonymously.
Telegram's "revolutionary privacy policy" has made it a safe haven for illegal and lurid activities, including the dissemination of revenge porn.

Summary:
While some social media and messaging platforms have taken steps in recent years to limit the spread of revenge porn (also known as non-consensual pornography), the problem continues to find new breeding ground in the internet’s shadows, like on encrypted messaging app, Telegram.
In recent months, following fears over WhatsApp‘s new privacy policies, hundreds of thousands of South Africans migrated to Telegram, where links to private groups circulate within communities, and joining them as an outsider is simple.
One such private group, the “Kinky Kallitz” Telegram account, has around 2000 members, who routinely share pornographic images and videos of young girls and women without their consent.
Users here have not only shared images taken without permission, but some have also provided the victims’ personal information, including names and phone numbers.
One of the victims, a Durban lingerie model, Jodi Nel, confronted the group’s members and was threatened with rape and physical abuse.
Another victim, who has an OnlyFans account, had all her content leaked on the group, and was also threatened with rape. She has now had to flee Cape Town to PE – fearing her life.
Research shows that there has been an alarming global increase in image-based abuse during the pandemic.
Yet current Cybersecurity laws – which are still being tabled in Parliament – are failing to protect the victims of this new form of technology-facilitated GBV.
Faced with legal hurdles and murky regulation, how can victims fight for control of the countless images that are still out there?
When a slippery network like Telegram is the locus of this abuse, a course for justice, both online and off, is difficult to chart.


Further information:
When WhatsApp informed users about its new terms of service and privacy policy on 8 January, it caused an outcry on social media which resulted in a media storm around WhatsApp privacy. Telegram product manager Pavel Durov said in the first week of January, Telegram surpassed 500 million monthly active users. He added that 25 million new users joined Telegram in the first three days since the WhatsApp privacy policy update.
This trend has continued, with millions of South Africans now subscribing to Telegram.
The app prides itself at being being private, as users can remain anonymoius on groups without having any of their personal details displayed - unlike Whatsapp which is reliant on one's cellphone number.
It's this anonymity which Telegram provides that has resulted in the mushrooming of groups which facilitate illegal and nefarious behaviour.

Press Release:


Naked Truth about Private Messaging Apps
They’ve spent months living in fear for their lives, faced death and rape threats and been stalked online and in person – all by strangers who’ve stolen their most intimate images and shared them with thousands of other nameless, faceless group members on an encrypted social media messaging app that prides itself on its privacy and security. Carte Blanche goes inside some of the local chat groups facilitating non-consensual pornography and image-based abuse and meets the women who’ve survived this invasive ordeal to tell their stories.
Producer: Latashia Naidoo | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

VIZ: 04:02:23:02 - 04:02:48:10 - “Number one is that it’s a borderless crime… jurisdiction-wise, it’s difficult to identify where the material is, to get court orders specifically on that environment.”

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Image-based sexual abuse - Inside the Telegram groups spreading revenge porn Rape videos, revenge porn, and child porn - just some of the content that's being shared on scores of local private Telegram groups which pride themselves at shaming and doxing women, anonymously. Telegram's "revolutionary privacy policy" has made it a safe haven for illegal and lurid activities, including the dissemination of revenge porn.
metadata.Summary: While some social media and messaging platforms have taken steps in recent years to limit the spread of revenge porn (also known as non-consensual pornography), the problem continues to find new breeding ground in the internet’s shadows, like on encrypted messaging app, Telegram. In recent months, following fears over WhatsApp‘s new privacy policies, hundreds of thousands of South Africans migrated to Telegram, where links to private groups circulate within communities, and joining them as an outsider is simple. One such private group, the “Kinky Kallitz” Telegram account, has around 2000 members, who routinely share pornographic images and videos of young girls and women without their consent. Users here have not only shared images taken without permission, but some have also provided the victims’ personal information, including names and phone numbers. One of the victims, a Durban lingerie model, Jodi Nel, confronted the group’s members and was threatened with rape and physical abuse. Another victim, who has an OnlyFans account, had all her content leaked on the group, and was also threatened with rape. She has now had to flee Cape Town to PE – fearing her life. Research shows that there has been an alarming global increase in image-based abuse during the pandemic. Yet current Cybersecurity laws – which are still being tabled in Parliament – are failing to protect the victims of this new form of technology-facilitated GBV. Faced with legal hurdles and murky regulation, how can victims fight for control of the countless images that are still out there? When a slippery network like Telegram is the locus of this abuse, a course for justice, both online and off, is difficult to chart.
metadata.Further information: When WhatsApp informed users about its new terms of service and privacy policy on 8 January, it caused an outcry on social media which resulted in a media storm around WhatsApp privacy. Telegram product manager Pavel Durov said in the first week of January, Telegram surpassed 500 million monthly active users. He added that 25 million new users joined Telegram in the first three days since the WhatsApp privacy policy update. This trend has continued, with millions of South Africans now subscribing to Telegram. The app prides itself at being being private, as users can remain anonymoius on groups without having any of their personal details displayed - unlike Whatsapp which is reliant on one's cellphone number. It's this anonymity which Telegram provides that has resulted in the mushrooming of groups which facilitate illegal and nefarious behaviour.
